newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Zeneca talk set to run and run.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Zeneca talk set to run and run.

text.p: Speculation about the future of bioscience specialist Zeneca Group Plc, which saw its already soaring share price reach new heights this week, is likely to run and run, weary analysts said on Friday.

Rumours of an outright takeover, asset swap or partial merger involving Germany's drugs and chemicals group Bayer AG pushed Zeneca shares up 82.5 pence at one point on Thursday as speculation swirled.

An outright denial by Bayer helped the stock ease back 21.5 pence to 15.68 pounds by midday on Friday, but analysts believe Zeneca's fundamental attractions and momentum in the fast-evolving drugs industry mean the respite will only be temporary.

In the wake of the merger which created Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc last year and plans by Switzerland's Sandoz AG and Ciba-Geigy AG to get together as Novartis, analysts are reluctant to put their heads above the parapet and say a merger or takeover won't happen.
"Never say never," said an analyst at a merchant bank who asked not to be named, but he added that in the immediate future "it doesn't make sense."

With a ballooning price tag of around $30 billion, analysts said Zeneca may well be safe from any predator other than the cash-rich Swiss group Roche AG, which is still smarting from losing its number one position at home to Novartis.
Yamaichi international analyst Erling Refsum said the bid talk was effectively acting a "poison pill," actually protecting Zeneca from takeover.
And a merger, such as with Bayer's complementary pharmaceutical and agrochemical operations, also appears to be ruled out by scarcely concealed hosility to the idea among Zeneca's management.

"It is a case of do Zeneca want to merge?" the merchant bank analyst said, adding that a merger was unlikley to offer anything better than the annual 15 percent pretax profit growth rates predicted for the company.

But another analyst at a U.K. brokerage, who also asked not to be identified, said the problems facing Zeneca were in the longer-term as it competed with giants like Novartis, whose R&D spend had actually gone up.
"It really means that for a medium-sized player like Zeneca it will be hard to get the new products developed and through as fast as other major players can," she said.
She added that even at current levels Zeneca was not expensive given its product portfolio and pipeline. A takeover would be "earnings enhancing very quickly indeed" for a predator.
And with two highly saleable non-core operations, agro-chemicals and specialty chemicals worth an estimated 3 1/2 billion stg, the group's price tag would not be as high as it first appears.
Yamaichi's Refsum said the rumours would carry on circulating for some time "but it is a matter of how long people will be able to believe in them."

But with investors who missed Glaxo Plc's snatching of Wellcome Plc in March 1995 terrified of losing out again, analysts said the risk in Zeneca's shares will continue to be on the upside for some time to come.
